truthAudit.Summary: Run 2 captured several true vulnerabilities with source-backed evidence, but it missed seven ground-truth issues, used incorrect CWE or severity labels on several found issues, and included one previous finding with no ground-truth mapping.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Format string in debug log using runtime format
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified the runtime log format and the vulnerable printf call, matching SC-V3-001. The severity was undercalled relative to the ground truth, but the vulnerability itself was present in the audited answer.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Integer overflow in factorial calculation for large input
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified the factorial result multiplication loop as an integer overflow risk, matching SC-V3-002. The severity was undercalled, but the vulnerability was found.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Use-after-free of memory pool scratch while thread pool tasks are pending
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified scratch capture, thread-pool enqueue, and memory-pool cleanup, matching SC-V3-003. The severity was undercalled, but the vulnerability was found.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: OS command injection in config validator path
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified the validator command built from configured values and passed to system(), matching SC-V3-004. The CWE and severity labels were not the ground-truth labels, but the vulnerability was found.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Stack buffer overflow in evaluate_expression for long input
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified strcpy into the fixed input_buffer_ for long expressions, matching SC-V3-005. The severity was overstated relative to the ground truth.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Data race in ThreadSafeCounter increment and get
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified the unsafe read before lock and the unlocked get, matching SC-V3-006. The CWE and severity labels were not the ground-truth labels, but the vulnerability was found.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Admin emergency override bypass after failed login attempts
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified the login_attempts_ greater than five condition, EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE branch, and authenticated_ assignment, matching SC-V3-007. The CWE and severity labels were not the ground-truth labels, and the severity was overstated.
The audited answer did not identify the path traversal issue in configuration loading based on config_dir_ plus filename in load_config.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Unbounded strcpy into fixed 256-byte parser expression buffer
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified the 256-byte parser buffer and unbounded strcpy into expression_buffer_, matching SC-V3-009. The CWE label was not the ground-truth label, but the vulnerability was found.
The previous answer identified the hardcoded ADMIN_SECRET value, matching SC-V3-010.

The previous answer identified mt19937 and uniform_int_distribution in a 1000 to 9999 range for session tokens, matching SC-V3-011. The CWE and severity labels were not the ground-truth labels, but the vulnerability was found.
The audited answer did not identify the thread-unsafe static cached_time / localtime issue in logging.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: OS command injection in emergency audit logging from environment temp directory
Items.Notes: The previous answer captured the temporary-directory environment handling and system call in the emergency audit path, but framed the issue as command injection rather than the ground-truth insecure temporary file handling vulnerability. It therefore only partially covers SC-V3-013.
The audited answer did not identify persistent authentication state based on authenticated_, login_attempts_, and session_token_ as a distinct vulnerability.
The audited answer did not identify the unhandled std::stod exception risk in handle_variable_command.
The audited answer did not identify the integer underflow in memory-pool block splitting. The use-after-free finding is a different vulnerability.
The audited answer did not identify unbounded recursion in the parser around parse_expression, parse_factor, and PAREN_OPEN.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Data race on expression result cache without mutex protection
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified result_cache_ access without the declared cache_mutex_ under thread-pool task scheduling, matching SC-V3-018. The CWE label was not the ground-truth label, but the vulnerability was found.
The audited answer did not identify the TOCTOU issue in configuration loading involving filesystem existence check, sleep, and file open.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Integer division by zero in route score for empty input
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified division by token_length with zero-length input, matching SC-V3-020.
